name: True-shape catalogue packshot
purpose: show a frame exactly as it is, with no perspective exaggeration of the front vs the temples
how: 100 mm macro (or 85-135 mm) from ~40-60 cm, f/11; DOF at 40 cm is only ~8 mm (c=0.03 mm) so stack 5-10 frames from lens front to temple tips; camera at bridge height, 5-15 deg above for the top bar; lens profile correction on
prompt_hint: 'product photo of eyeglasses, 100 mm macro lens from a distance, true-to-shape frame, sharp from front to temple tips, soft gradient background'
limits: AI cannot be trusted for product geometry: composite the real kit cutout; stacking needs a still subject

name: Hinge / logo macro insert
purpose: material truth: screws, acetate layers, engraved logo
how: 1:1 macro, f/8-f/11 (DOF ~1-1.3 mm, from 2Nc(1+m)/m^2), 10-30 stacked frames; long macro (100 mm+) for working distance so a softbox gradient can reflect in polished metal; effective aperture loses ~2 stops at 1:1
prompt_hint: 'extreme macro of an acetate eyeglass hinge, focus-stacked, every screw sharp, soft gradient reflection'
limits: single AI image will invent screw counts and logos; dust and fingerprints show at 1:1

name: Try-on portrait, eyes sharp
purpose: flattering, trustworthy face with glasses and a soft shop background
how: 85 mm f/2-2.8 from ~1.5 m (MCU/CU); DOF at f/2 ~3.5 cm: focus on the near eye/lens front; temple tips may soften; keep the face out of the frame corners
prompt_hint: 'portrait of a woman trying on glasses, 85 mm lens, photographed from 1.5 m, f/2, shallow depth of field, eyes in sharp focus'
limits: closer than ~1 m reintroduces the big-nose effect even with an 85 mm crop

name: Face with the whole frame sharp
purpose: show the full frame on the face (front + temple to ear) for fit explanations
how: 85 mm f/5.6 at 1.5 m gives ~10 cm DOF; 3/4 or profile view; light so the far temple separates
prompt_hint: '85 mm, f/5.6, the entire eyeglass frame sharp from lenses to ear tips, three-quarter view'
limits: background less blurred; separate with light/colour instead

name: Melt the background behind a person
purpose: isolate a customer from a busy street/shop at the same framing
how: step back and use 135-200 mm instead of opening a 50 mm wider: at equal subject size DOF is almost the same, but the distant background blurs more with the longer lens; keep >= 3-5 m between subject and background
prompt_hint: 'shot from far away with a 200 mm telephoto lens, background reduced to soft colour, subject sharp'
limits: needs space; heavy compression flattens the face slightly

name: Environmental portrait in the shop
purpose: staff/owner in context, shop readable around them
how: 35 mm from 2-3 m at f/2.8-4; subject in the central third (edges of a 35 mm frame stretch faces); level camera so verticals of display cases stay straight
prompt_hint: '35 mm environmental portrait of an optician in a small eyewear shop, level camera, straight vertical lines, subject centred'
limits: do not move closer than ~1.5 m for a face; corners distort

name: Deep-focus establishing shot
purpose: everything from foreground to horizon acceptably sharp
how: 24 mm at f/8 focused at the hyperfocal distance H ~2.4 m (sharp from ~1.2 m to infinity, c=0.03 mm); 35 mm f/8 H ~5.1 m
prompt_hint: 'wide establishing shot, 24 mm, deep focus, everything sharp from the foreground railing to the horizon'
limits: phone sensors already have deep focus; c must shrink if the frame is cropped heavily for 9:16

name: Straight verticals on a vertical storefront
purpose: professional architecture look in 9:16 where converging verticals are very visible
how: keep the camera level and shift the lens (or shoot wider, level, and crop the upper part); or keystone-correct in post; avoid pitching the camera up
prompt_hint: 'front view of the shop facade, level camera, vertical lines perfectly parallel, architectural photography'
limits: post-correction stretches the top; leave margin
use_for: closure notices with a shop photo

name: Miniature ('toy town') intro
purpose: make Hua Hin streets look like a diorama for a playful opener
how: high viewpoint (bird's-eye ~30-60 deg down), tilted focus plane or a post blur that grows smoothly above and below a horizontal band following the ground plane; boost saturation and contrast
prompt_hint: 'tilt-shift photograph of a beach town street from above, miniature effect, narrow band of focus, toy-like'
limits: blur must match the depth gradient or the scale illusion fails (Held2010: some blur approximations do not work)

name: Peephole / door-camera POV
purpose: comic or suspense POV of someone at the shop door
how: circular fisheye look (8-10 mm full-frame equivalent, equisolid/equidistant mapping); lines through the centre straight; vignette to black outside the circle
prompt_hint: 'circular fisheye view through a door peephole, curved walls, person at the door in the centre'
limits: never on product geometry; AI often bends only part of the image

name: Uncorrected-vision POV
purpose: let viewers feel blurred distance vision before the new glasses
how: defocus blur that increases with distance (near objects sharp for a myope), lower contrast at distance; then rack to sharp when the glasses go on
prompt_hint: 'point-of-view of a short-sighted person: near hands sharp, street signs in the distance blurred'
limits: simulation is illustrative, not clinical; label as such in health content

name: Rack focus from reflection to face
purpose: move attention from the lens surface (coating reflection) to the eye behind it
how: long lens, wide aperture (f/2-2.8), focus pulled from the lens front to the eye (~1-2 cm apart at MCU distance means a tiny pull at 85 mm f/2); in rig.js use cam.rack
prompt_hint: video: 'slow rack focus from the reflection on the lens to the eye behind it'
limits: AI video seldom performs a true focus pull; may need two clips crossfaded

name: Phone-viewing focal-length choice
purpose: make faces and products look natural on small screens viewed at ~30 cm
how: prefer 70-100 mm-equivalent framing for people/products (Cooper et al. recommend longer focal lengths for small, close-viewed images; median Flickr SLR focal length 68 mm); keep 24-35 mm for scene-setting
prompt_hint: 'medium close-up, 85 mm lens look, natural proportions'
limits: recommendation derived from print-viewing experiments; not tested on IG audiences

name: Deliberate close wide-angle comedy face
purpose: exaggerate a character's surprise or a selfie joke
how: 24 mm or wider from 30-40 cm: nose x1.2+ relative to ears; use only when the joke is the distortion
prompt_hint: 'comic close-up selfie, wide-angle lens very close, exaggerated nose, funny expression'
limits: lowers trust/attractiveness ratings (Bryan 2012) - never on a customer or a product hero

name: Natural motion in shop video
purpose: cinematic, flicker-free motion under shop lighting
how: 25 fps at 1/50 s (180 deg) under 50 Hz mains lighting; 24 fps at 1/48 may flicker under some lights; check LED panels
limits: AI video ignores shutter settings; this is for real filming and for choosing rig motion blur

name: Crisp staccato action
purpose: make a fast action (frame snapping open, sunglasses tossed) crisp and energetic
how: 45-90 deg shutter (1/192-1/96 s at 24 fps); more light needed
prompt_hint: 'crisp fast action, no motion blur, frozen water droplets'

name: Subtle vignette to hold the eye
purpose: keep attention on the centred product
how: darken corners 0.3-0.5 stop (natural cos^4 falloff is ~0.4 stop at 20 deg off-axis); avoid visible rings
limits: heavy vignette reads retro/toy; conflicts with logo corners

name: Before/after flare to sell AR coating
how: 'before': bright point light at the frame edge producing ghost images and veiling glare across an uncoated lens; 'after': same light, clean view; keep light position identical
prompt_hint: 'split image: left, uncoated lens with strong reflections and ghosting from a lamp; right, same scene through an anti-reflective coated lens, clear'
limits: camera-lens flare and spectacle-lens reflections are different systems; claims about coating performance need lens-maker data

name: Deliberate chromatic aberration
purpose: vintage/glitch mood in a music beat clip
how: lateral CA: shift R and B channels outward toward the edges (none at the centre); keep the product centred and clean
prompt_hint: 'vintage lens with slight chromatic aberration at the edges'
limits: on metal frames, fringes read as dirt or bad quality; never on catalogue shots
